drug_class: PCSK9 inhibitor (a type of cholesterol-lowering injection)
purpose: Evolocumab is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) in your blood. It is used when diet changes and other cholesterol medicines like statins are not enough, or if you have a genetic condition causing very high cholesterol. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes in people who already have heart disease.
how_it_works: Your liver has special proteins called PCSK9 that break down the receptors responsible for removing bad cholesterol from your blood. Evolocumab blocks PCSK9, which means your liver can keep more of those receptors working. With more active receptors, your body removes more bad cholesterol from your bloodstream, lowering your levels significantly.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are redness, bruising, or soreness at the injection site. Some people experience cold or flu-like symptoms, back pain, or joint aches. Runny nose and headache have also been reported.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine in those situations is not fully established. Let your doctor know about all other medicines you take. If you have a latex allergy, check with your pharmacist since some delivery devices may contain latex. Rarely, serious allergic reactions can occur — seek emergency help if you have difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, or a severe rash.
typical_dosing: Evolocumab is given as an injection under the skin, usually in the belly, thigh, or upper arm. The typical dose is either 140 mg injected every two weeks, or 420 mg injected once a month. Your doctor will decide which schedule is best for you. The medicine comes in a prefilled auto-injector pen or syringe that is easy to use at home.
